states.verdict: These two title bars are the same bar: 32 px band, Library toggle at 17 px in, View button ending 17 px from the right, both icon groups matching to within one device pixel, the same #8C8C8C title, the same 26 px stats band under the same full-bleed 1-device-px #DFDFDF rule, the same #4A4A4A/#8C8C8C number-and-label pair, both triplets centred dead on 1440. states.name: empty
states.gap: A sets the stats numbers heaviest of anything in the frame: the '0' carries 98 dark px to B's 71 and '< 1 min' 232 to B's 187 at identical #4A4A4A and identical cap height (~35% more ink, semibold vs medium), so on an empty document the loudest mark on the whole 2880x1800 sheet is a counter reading zero. states.gapTheirs: B draws the caret through the first glyph: caret occupies cols 626-631 while the 'S' of 'Start writing…' starts at col 624, so 6 device px (3 logical) of blue sit on top of the letter and bisect it — at 100% the S reads as a broken character. A's caret ends at col 624 and the S begins at 625: flush, no collision. B also titles an unsaved document 'Untitled.md', inventing a file extension for a file that does not exist.
states.verdict: The two bars are the same bars — same 32/26 px heights, same #4A4A4A number over #8C8C8C label, same Library and View icons to the pixel — so this comes down to two mistakes, and only B makes them. Opening B's empty document, the very first thing your eye lands on is a caret slicing the S of the placeholder in half; that is the one pixel a writer stares at before typing and B got it wrong. And the title bar tells you the document is called 'Untitled.md' when you have never saved anything — three characters of technical noise in the one strip whose whole job is to say nothing. A's cost is a stats bar that shouts its zeros in semibold; B's cost is a broken glyph and a lie in the title, and I would rather mute a bar than fix a caret.

states.name: typing
states.gap: A's dimmed bar is the louder of the two at the exact moment it is meant to be at a third: 91,143 total ink units vs B's 80,057 over the identical 500x20 device-px window centred on the stats block (~14% more ink), and it sits on a 2-level darker ground (#F7F7F7 vs #F9F9F9) so its label grey #CECECE clears the page by only 41 levels against B's #CFCFCF at 42 — A buys its hierarchy with insistence, not with recession. Its ink also starts one device row higher (1763 vs 1764), leaving the run 1.5 CSS px above the bar's optical centre against B's 1.25.
states.gapTheirs: B has no weight step worth the name between a number and its label. Measured as ink per px inside each run: B's '961' 20.1 against 'characters' 10.8 (1.86x) and '188' 20.8 against 'words' 10.9 (1.91x); A's are 22.8 vs 10.5 (2.17x) and 23.7 vs 10.1 (2.35x). The colour step is identical in both (#B6->#CF vs #B5->#CE), so this is purely weight: B's 'bold' number is barely bolder than its label, and '188 words' reads as one flat grey phrase you must actually stop and parse instead of a figure you catch peripherally.
states.verdict: There is almost nothing between these: both have taken the title bar away completely with no residue above y=232, both draw a 1px full-bleed hairline at the same y=1748 at 3.6% of ground, both give the bar the same 26 CSS px, both centre the same three stats on the window at x=1440, neither leaks a scrollbar. So it comes down to whether the bar is still readable at a glance once it has been dimmed, and only A's is: A's number stands at 2.2-2.35x the ink of its label, B's at 1.86-1.91x, which is the difference between clocking '188' out of the corner of your eye and having to look at it. B's flatter bar is quieter by 14%, and it bought that quiet by making the one thing on the bar you actually want stop working.

states.gap: B draws a persistent scrollbar — a solid #A8A8A8 rail 6px wide (3 logical px) hard against the right window edge, running y=68 to y=1100 — still sitting there with a modal palette open; A's right edge is empty page. states.gapTheirs: A guillotines the palette's last row worse: the panel's hard bottom edge (y=960) lands 9px into a 17px glyph band, so 'Dark or Light Appearance' is sliced through the middle of its x-height, versus B's cut at y=962 leaving 16px of an 18px band — a clip just under the baseline that still reads. Neither panel fades or masks the cut; A's just shows decapitated letterforms.
states.verdict: These are the same two bars to within a pixel, so the choice comes down to what each adds that nobody asked for. B hangs a grey rail down the right margin of the page — the one piece of chrome a writing app exists to hide — and then washes its own search prompt out to #BA next to a #8C magnifier, a tonal mismatch on a single baseline that a typographer sees before reading the word. A's sin is smaller and cosmetic: its palette ends by cutting a line of type through the waist instead of below the baseline. A rail you stare at all day beats a clipped row you glance at once.
